label: rem:toric-chemical-groebner-geometry
title: Gröbner test sets, Sturmfels–Thomas enthalpy normal forms, and Birch mass-action toric equilibria
html:
Because \eta_2 \approx 1.77 \times 10^{-6} \ll 1, Layer \mathcal{L}_2 nuclear cores remain invariant across ambient chemical transformations, reducing molecular reaction stoichiometry to integer lattice geometry and toric commutative algebra [deloera-hemmecke-koeppe2013, craciun-dickenstein-shiu-sturmfels2009].

Smith normal form, lattice saturation, and the toric test-set hierarchy

Computing \ker_{\mathbb{Z}}(A_{\mathrm{chem}}) via Hermite or Smith normal form U A_{\mathrm{chem}} V = \mathrm{diag}(d_1, \dots, d_r, 0, \dots, 0) yields a saturated free sublattice of \mathbb{Z}^M: even when invariant factors carry prime torsion in \mathbb{Z}^E / A_{\mathrm{chem}}\mathbb{Z}^M (for instance \mathrm{SNF}(A_{\mathrm{CHO}}) = \mathrm{diag}(1, 1, 2) owing to even hydrogen parity across (\mathrm{C},\mathrm{H}_2,\mathrm{O}_2,\mathrm{CO},\mathrm{CO}_2,\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O},\mathrm{CH}_4)), the kernel \ker_{\mathbb{Z}}(A_{\mathrm{chem}}) is torsion-free and generates the prime toric ideal

  I_{A_{\mathrm{chem}}} := \bigl\langle x^{\nu_+} - x^{\nu_-} \;:\; \nu_+ - \nu_- \in \ker_{\mathbb{Z}}(A_{\mathrm{chem}})\bigr\rangle \subset k[x_1, \dots, x_M].

Inside \ker_{\mathbb{Z}}(A_{\mathrm{CHO}}) \cong \mathbb{Z}^4, the support-minimal elementary circuits \mathrm{Circ}(A_{\mathrm{CHO}}), the universal Gröbner basis \mathrm{UGB}(I_{A_{\mathrm{CHO}}}), and the conformal-minimal Graver basis \mathcal{G}(A_{\mathrm{CHO}}) [deloera-hemmecke-koeppe2013, hemmecke-koeppe-weismantel2014] form a strict chain of unoriented reaction pairs:

  \bigl|\mathrm{Circ}(A_{\mathrm{CHO}})\bigr| = 20
  \;<\;
  \bigl|\mathrm{UGB}(I_{A_{\mathrm{CHO}}})\bigr| = 32
  \;<\;
  \bigl|\mathcal{G}(A_{\mathrm{CHO}})\bigr| = 33.

Zero-temperature Sturmfels–Thomas reduction and finite-temperature Birch equilibria

At T \to 0, minimizing molar enthalpy h_f^\top u over the discrete stoichiometric fiber polytope P_b \cap \mathbb{N}^M = \{u \in \mathbb{N}^M : A_{\mathrm{chem}} u = b\} reduces to monomial normal-form division modulo the h_f-oriented Gröbner test set [sturmfels-thomas1997]. On the inventory b = (2, 8, 4)^\top (17 feasible integer points in P_b \cap \mathbb{N}^7), unburned synthesis gas u_0 = (0,4,1,2,0,0,0) (2\,\mathrm{CO} + 4\,\mathrm{H}_2 + \mathrm{O}_2) reduces confluently in three exothermic binomial rewrites to the unique integer-programming global minimum u^* = (2,0,0,0,0,4,0) (2\,\mathrm{C} + 4\,\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}).

At finite temperature T > 0, entropic mixing lifts the discrete boundary optimum into the positive interior \mathbb{R}_{>0}^M. Detailed-balance mass-action kinetics [horn-jackson1972, feinberg1972, gatermann-huber2002, craciun-dickenstein-shiu-sturmfels2009] imposes the shifted toric binomial equations

  x^{\nu_+} = K_{\mathrm{eq}}(\nu_+ - \nu_-)\,x^{\nu_-},
  \qquad
  K_{\mathrm{eq}}(v) = \exp\!\left(-\frac{v^\top g^\circ}{R T}\right),

parameterized by elemental log-fugacity dual potentials y \in \mathbb{R}^E via x_j(y) = \exp\bigl((A_{\mathrm{chem}}^\top y)_j - g^\circ_j / (R T)\bigr) on the affine toric variety V(I_{A_{\mathrm{chem}}}) = \mathrm{Spec}\,\mathbb{C}[\mathbb{N} A_{\mathrm{chem}}]. Because the Legendre potential \Phi(y) = \sum_{j=1}^M x_j(y) - b^\top y has strictly positive-definite Hessian \nabla^2 \Phi(y) = A_{\mathrm{chem}}\,\mathrm{diag}(x(y))\,A_{\mathrm{chem}}^\top \succ 0 on \mathbb{R}_{>0}^M, Birch's theorem [birch1963] guarantees a unique positive equilibrium x^* \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}^M in every stoichiometric compatibility class A_{\mathrm{chem}} x = b.
